cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose delegate is a LowestValueIndicator that returns the minimum of the last 3 values of the source indicator. For a source indicator with values [10, 8, 12, 5, 7] the returned indicator should produce values [10, 8, 8, 5, 5] at indexes 0‑4 respectively.
cases.description: Verify that `lowest(3)` creates a NumericIndicator wrapping a LowestValueIndicator and that it correctly calculates the lowest value over the specified window.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown because barCount must be greater than 0
cases.description: Verify that calling `lowest(0)` on a NumericIndicator rejects a zero window size and throws an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown because barCount must be positive
cases.description: Ensure that a negative barCount is considered invalid and results in an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose delegate is a LowestValueIndicator that returns the minimum of all values seen so far (window limited by series start). For a source indicator with values [4, 9, 2, 7, 5] the returned indicator should produce values [4, 4, 2, 2, 2] at indexes 0‑4 respectively.
cases.description: Check that when barCount is larger than the series length, the indicator correctly uses the available values up to the current index instead of throwing an error.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose delegate is a LowestValueIndicator that simply mirrors the source values. For a source indicator with values [3, 6, 1, 8] the returned indicator should produce values [3, 6, 1, 8] at indexes 0‑3 respectively.
cases.description: Validate that a window size of 1 returns the original indicator values unchanged.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose delegate is a LowestValueIndicator applied to the derived indicator (source + 2). For a source indicator with values [5, 1, 4, 9, 2] the derived indicator (source.plus(2)) yields [7, 3, 6, 11, 4]; the lowest(3) over this derived series should produce values [7, 3, 3, 3, 3] at indexes 0‑4 respectively.
cases.description: Confirm that `lowest` works on a NumericIndicator that has been transformed (e.g., via `plus`) and that the window calculation uses the transformed values.
